title: Finiteness of global Ext between coherent complexes on proper algebraic spaces
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $X$ a proper algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Proper means separated, of finite type, and universally closed: the diagonal is a closed immersion, the morphism is quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and every algebraic-space base change is closed on underlying spaces. On the small etale site of $X$, work in $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A module sheaf is coherent if on every Noetherian affine etale chart it is associated to a finitely generated module; association on a chart $\operatorname{Spec}R$ gives the etale sheaf with value $B\otimes_RN$ on affine etale charts $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$. Let $E$ have coherent cohomology vanishing in all sufficiently large degrees, and let $F$ have coherent cohomology vanishing in all sufficiently negative degrees. For every integer $n$ the $A$-module
$$\operatorname{Ext}^n_{\mathcal O_X}(E,F):=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(E,F[n])$$
is finitely generated. The $A$-action is induced by the structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$.

source.place: Tag 0D0T (lemma-ext-finite), for K in D^-_Coh and L in D^+_Coh.

proof.text: Put $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and let $f:X\to Y$ be the structure morphism. The single affine chart makes $Y$ locally Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] makes $Y$ quasi-compact. To check local Noetherianity of $X$, take an etale scheme atlas and refine it to affine charts $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ on which the map to $Y$ is given by a finitely generated $A$-algebra, as in the definition of locally finite type on charts. Each $B_i$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. These charts form a locally Noetherian atlas, which is precisely local Noetherianity of $X$. This is the chartwise argument of Tag 04ZK, not an extra assertion about a specified global scheme cover.

source.place: Tag 04ZK (lemma-locally-finite-type-locally-noetherian), proof by scheme charts; algebra.tex Tag 00FN.

proof.text: Form $G=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(E,F)$. The local Noetherianity just proved, the coherent cohomology of both arguments, the upper cohomological bound on $E$, and the lower bound on $F$ are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-space-coherent-derived-internal-hom]. Hence $G$ has coherent cohomology and lies in $D^+(\mathcal O_X)$. No perfectness of $E$ and no bound above on $F$ is used.

Apply [lem-sfb-proper-space-coherent-derived-image] to $f:X\to Y$ and $G$. The target is the Noetherian scheme $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $f$ is proper by the item hypothesis, and $G$ is bounded below with coherent cohomology by step 2. Thus $T=Rf_*G$ is bounded below with coherent cohomology on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$. In the cited Stacks lemma the auxiliary base scheme is taken to be $S=Y$, so the support condition concerns properness over the actual target.

By the closed structure of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal], for every $L\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ the functor $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(L,-)$ is right adjoint to $-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}L$; composing with its symmetry $\sigma$, $M\mapsto R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(E,M)$ is a right adjoint $H_E$ of $E\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}-$, as the sections model requires. Use [lem-sfb-derived-internal-hom-sections-model] for this $H_E$ on $(X_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_X)$: for every integer $n$ it gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(E,F[n])\cong H^nR\Gamma(X,G)$. Let $h$ be the morphism from $(Y_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_Y)$ to the point ringed by $A=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$. Its module direct image is global sections with this $A$-action, and $(hf)_*=h_*f_*$ is global sections on $X$ with its structure-morphism action. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to $f,h$. More explicitly, take a K-injective representative $I$ of $G$ and a K-injective resolution $j:f_*I\to J$ on $Y$. The cited normalization says that $h_*j:\Gamma(X,I)\to\Gamma(Y,J)$ is a quasi-isomorphism representing $\kappa_{h,f,G}$. Both complexes and this map carry the $A$-action through $h$, so this is the comparison $R\Gamma(X,G)\cong R\Gamma(Y,T)$ in $D(A)$, with $T=Rf_*G$. All sites are small in a common containing universe. Taking cohomology identifies the desired Ext group with $H^nR\Gamma(Y,T)$; compatibility of the first identification with scalars is checked in step 6.

source.place: Tag 08JA (lemma-section-RHom-over-U), with shifts, and Tag 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition); these realize the displayed equalities in 0D0T.

proof.text: Choose $a\in\mathbf Z$ with $\mathcal H^q(T)=0$ for $q<a$, and a bounded-below representative, using [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Module sheaves on the small ringed site and $A$-modules are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] and [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian]. Global sections is additive and left exact, since kernels and finite products of sheaves are computed on sections. Therefore [thm-sp-truncation-e2], applied to this functor with values in $A$-modules, gives the convergent spectral sequence $E_2^{p,q}=H^p(Y_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal H^q(T))\Rightarrow H^{p+q}R\Gamma(Y,T)$ with $p\geq0,q\geq a$. For fixed total degree $n$, only $0\leq p\leq n-a$ can contribute. Its abutment filtration satisfies $F^0H^n=H^n$, $F^pH^n=0$ for $p\geq n-a+1$, and $F^pH^n/F^{p+1}H^n\cong E_\infty^{p,n-p}$. Each $\mathcal H^q(T)$ is, on the affine chart $Y$ itself, the etale sheaf associated to a finite $A$-module $M_q$, by the coherence convention. Its values $B\otimes_AM_q$ on affine etale $\operatorname{Spec}B\to Y$ are those of the associated sheaf $(\widetilde{M_q})_{\mathrm{et}}$, so it is the etale sheaf of a quasi-coherent module and [lem-sc-etale-affine-qcoherent] kills its abelian etale cohomology in positive degrees. The derived functors $R^p\Gamma$ in the spectral sequence are computed by injective module resolutions; after forgetting the $A$-action they are $R^p$ of evaluation at the terminal object $Y$ on $\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)$, which has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives], and [lem-pe-ringed-site-derived-evaluation-slice] with $W=Y$ (whose slice site is $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$) identifies them with abelian etale cohomology of the underlying abelian sheaf. Hence $E_2^{p,q}=0$ for $p>0$, while $E_2^{0,q}=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal H^q(T))=M_q$.

source.place: Tag 015J (lemma-two-ss-complex-functor), second spectral sequence; spaces-cohomology.tex Tag 07UB (lemma-coherent-Noetherian); etale affine acyclicity as in lem-sc-etale-affine-qcoherent.

proof.text: Only the column $p=0$ survives in step 5: every differential into or out of that column has zero other endpoint. Put $H^n=H^nR\Gamma(Y,T)$. For $n\geq a$, start at the zero filtration term $F^{n-a+1}H^n$ and descend: each positive-$p$ graded piece vanishes, hence $F^pH^n=F^{p+1}H^n$ for $p\geq1$ and $F^1H^n=0$. Thus $H^n=F^0H^n/F^1H^n\cong E_\infty^{0,n}=E_2^{0,n}=M_n$. For $n<a$, the bound $F^pH^n=0$ for $p\geq n-a+1$ already applies at $p=0$, so $H^n=0=M_n$. These are isomorphisms of $A$-modules: step 5 takes place in $A$-modules and the Leray comparison in step 4 is in $D(A)$. For scalar compatibility in the global-Hom comparison, represent $F$ by a K-injective complex $J$. For each $r\in A$, multiplication $r\,\mathrm{id}_J$ is a chain map representing $r\,\mathrm{id}_F$. The naturality in K-injective target complexes stated in [lem-sfb-derived-internal-hom-sections-model] identifies postcomposition by this map with multiplication by $r$ on $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(E^\bullet,J)$. Thus the induced isomorphism on cohomology respects exactly the structure-morphism action on Ext. Hence step 4 identifies the desired Ext module with the finite module $M_n$. Transporting a finite generating set along this $A$-linear isomorphism proves the claim.
